name: Julius Caesar
hook: The man, the Ides, the Rubicon, and Shakespeare's most quotable assassination.

facts.label: the Ides of March
facts.statement: Julius Caesar was assassinated on the Ides of March — March 15, 44 B.C. — in the Roman Senate, despite a warning to beware that day.

facts.label: Marcus Brutus
facts.statement: Marcus Brutus, a friend Caesar had pardoned, helped lead the assassination; Shakespeare gives Caesar the line "Et tu, Brute?" as he dies.

facts.label: the Rubicon
facts.statement: In 49 B.C. Caesar crossed the Rubicon River into Italy, starting civil war — hence "the die is cast."

facts.label: the First Triumvirate
facts.statement: Caesar, Pompey and Crassus formed the First Triumvirate; after Crassus and Caesar's daughter Julia died, Pompey turned against him.

facts.label: Gaul
facts.statement: Caesar conquered Gaul by 50 B.C., the territory the Walloons inhabit, and wrote about Celts dyeing themselves blue with woad.

facts.label: Cleopatra
facts.statement: Cleopatra reportedly smuggled herself into Caesar's quarters in a rolled-up carpet, and Caesar put a gold statue of her in the temple of Venus Genetrix.

facts.label: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar
facts.statement: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar was performed by John Wilkes Booth and his brothers in 1864; "Et tu, Brute?" is the play's only Latin phrase.
